## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kammahetukathā* (Kv 8.11) is a debate located in the eighth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral]. The controversy examines the proposition that an arahant can fall away from arahantship on account of past actions (*kammahetu arahā arahattā parihāyati*) [Dutt 1945; Hazra 1994]. According to the commentary and doxographical traditions, this thesis was maintained by the Pubbaseliya and Sammitīya schools [Dutt 1945]. Opponents argued that if a person had slandered an arahant in a prior life (*purimabhava*), the karmic consequence of that past slander could cause them to retrogress from arahantship [Dutt 1945; Bareau 1955]. The orthodox Theravāda position rejects this claim, insisting that an arahant does not lose the state of liberation due to past deeds [Bareau 1955].
SuttaCentral records one translation into a modern language and lists no curated external parallels [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal links within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, particularly with the *Kathāvatthu*'s principal debate on the retrogression of an arahant, the *Parihānikathā* (Kv 1.2), with which it shares 63 passages (over 4,000 characters, notably §1.1–2.4 with Kv 1.2 §96.2–97.4) [DharmaNexus]. Further phraseological parallels in DharmaNexus connect the text to the *Sabbamidaṁkammatotikathā* (Kv 17.3) and several treatises of the *Paṭṭhāna* (*Kusalattika*, *Micchattaniyatattika*, and *Piṭṭhiduka*) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring automatic alignments with the Tibetan *Śatasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā*, though these constitute automated text matches rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
